claim: Notre-Dame entry is free for all and the official timed-entry reservation system is optional; slots release on a rolling 2-3 day window with new slots added throughout the day.
quote: The official reservation platform opens 2–3 days before the visit date... Slots are released on a rolling basis, typically only a few hours to two days before your desired visit

claim: Walk-in standby line at Notre-Dame moves quickly — typically under 12 minutes even on busy Sundays; cathedral free with optional reservations via Compagnon de Visite app.
quote: Visitors without reservations can always enter by joining the standby line... it usually moves quickly... on busy days (like Sunday) and have never waited more than 12 minutes

claim: Official 2026 Eiffel Tower adult prices: €23.50 second-floor lift, €14.80 second-floor stairs, €36.70 summit by lift.
quote: Second Floor by Lift: Adults €23.50... By Stairs: Adults €14.80... Summit by Lift: Adults €36.70

claim: Eiffel Tower lowest crowds 9-11am weekday and 8-10:30pm; one hour before sunset is the optimal single slot for golden-hour plus first sparkle show.
quote: Off-peak windows are typically 9–11am and 8–10:30pm... One hour before sunset is the best single time slot

claim: Eiffel Tower base has Paris's highest pickpocket density plus persistent fake-charity petition scams using photocopied deaf-mute charity logos.
quote: The fake charity collector is astonishingly common underneath the Eiffel Tower... photocopied logos from legitimate charities... charities for the deaf and mute

claim: Arc de Triomphe rooftop costs €22 April-September (€16 on Wednesdays), €16 October-March; open 10am-11pm summer, 10am-10:30pm winter.
quote: April 1 - September 30: Regular: €22, Wednesdays: €16... October 1 - March 31: Single ticket: €16

claim: Sacré-Cœur basilica is free; dome ticket €8 adult / €5 child, 300 narrow steps no elevator, last admission 8pm, tickets on-site only.
quote: Children (up to 15): €5, Adults (16+): €8... nearly 300 steps via a narrow staircase... tickets are purchased on-site only

claim: Sainte-Chapelle + Conciergerie combined ticket €30 (non-EEA) saves €5 vs separate tickets; standalone Sainte-Chapelle €22 non-EEA, €16 EEA.
quote: Outside EEA: €22... EEA residents: €16... combined Sainte-Chapelle + Conciergerie package costs €30 (outside EEA) or €23 (EEA residents)

claim: Sainte-Chapelle visit is time-stamped on the combo ticket; the Conciergerie portion can be visited any time during opening hours.
quote: Only the visit to the Sainte-Chapelle is time-stamped, the visit to the Conciergerie can take place at any time of day

claim: Centre Pompidou closed 22 September 2025 and will reopen in 2030 after a five-year renovation; major works begin early 2026.
quote: The building closes on September 22, 2025... The major renovation project... will begin in early 2026... The Centre Pompidou will reopen in 2030

claim: During the closure, Pompidou collection and programming travel via the 'Constellation' programme with major exhibitions at Grand Palais and Centre Pompidou-Metz.
quote: Renovation of the Centre Pompidou Paris from 2025 to 2030: the off-site programme

claim: Louvre 2026 admission is €22 for EEA residents, €32 for non-EEA visitors, free for under-18s and EEA residents under 26; first Friday after 6pm is free (except July/August).
quote: EEA residents/citizens: €22.00; Non-EEA visitors: €32.00; Under 18s and EEA residents under 26: Free... First Friday of each month after 6 PM (except July and August)

claim: Advance time-slot booking at the Louvre is strongly recommended (including for free-admission visitors) and is effectively the only way to guarantee entry; on-site purchase only works when attendance is low.
quote: Time-slot bookings are strongly recommended, including for free admission visitors, and only this advance booking guarantees you access to the museum

claim: The underground Carrousel entrance typically has 10–20 minute waits, and Porte des Lions (southwest, near the Seine) often has 5–15 minute waits but closes at 6pm and is shut Tuesdays.
quote: Carrousel du Louvre entrance delivers shorter queues than the iconic Pyramid, with wait times averaging 10-20 minutes... Porte des Lions on the southwest side near the Seine offers minimal waits of 5-15 minutes when open

claim: The Mona Lisa room holds fewer than 30 people in the first opening hour (9–10am) versus 200+ in peak afternoons; visitor numbers drop ~60% after 6pm on the Wednesday/Friday late nights (open until 9:45pm).
quote: The Mona Lisa room during opening hour often contains fewer than 30 people compared to 200+ during peak afternoon periods... Visitor numbers drop by roughly 60% after 6:00 PM

claim: Musée d'Orsay full ticket is €18 with a €12 reduced rate for the Thursday night opening after 6pm.
quote: Dedicated entrance tickets to the Musée d'Orsay are €18 per adult... the price of the night visit to the Musée d'Orsay is €12

claim: Musée d'Orsay is free to all on the first Sunday of every month, but reservation is mandatory and slots sell out within days of release for spring months.
quote: 1st Sunday of the month free · booking mandatory

claim: Musée de l'Orangerie costs €12.50 online (€11 on-site), and a combo ticket with Musée d'Orsay is €20 valid for 6 days — both house Monet's Water Lilies cycle in two purpose-built oval rooms.
quote: Tickets cost €12.50 per adult when purchased online, though on-site tickets cost €11... A combo ticket with Musée d'Orsay costs €20 (available at the Orangerie desk) and is valid for 6 days

claim: The Orangerie's Water Lilies are eight monumental Monet murals installed in two oval rooms exactly as the artist designed.
quote: Claude Monet's monumental Water Lilies (Les Nymphéas) — eight massive murals displayed in two purpose-built oval rooms exactly as Monet designed them

claim: Paris Museum Pass 2026 sells at €90 for 2 consecutive days, €109 for 4 days and €139 for 6 days, covering 50+ museums and monuments; the clock counts hours from first scan, not calendar days.
quote: €90 for 2 days, €109 for 4 days, and €139 for 6 days... unlimited access to over 50 museums and monuments... The clock starts at your first museum scan and counts hours, not calendar days

claim: Musée Picasso Paris (Hôtel Salé, 5 rue de Thorigny, Marais 3rd) is €16 full / €12 family, open Tue–Sun 9:30am–6pm, free first Sunday of the month with a late opening on the first Wednesday until 10pm.
quote: Regular price: €16; Family rate: €12 per adult... free on the 1st Sunday of the month. Evening hours on the first Wednesday of the month until 10 PM... From Tuesday to Sunday, the museum is open from 9:30 a.m. to 6 p.m

claim: Musée Rodin (Hôtel Biron) admission is around €13–14 including the sculpture garden, open Tue–Sun 10am–6:30pm; no separate garden-only ticket, and the on-site L'Augustine café sits inside the garden.
quote: open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6.30pm... You have to buy a full ticket that covers the museum and garden — there is no separate garden-only ticket available

claim: Musée du quai Branly–Jacques Chirac costs €14 full / €11 reduced, opens Tue–Sun 10:30am–7pm (Thursdays until 10pm), free for under-18s, EU 18–25 and on the first Sunday of the month.
quote: Admission to the Quai Branly Museum is €14, while the discounted price is €11... Tuesday to Sunday: from 10:30 am to 7 pm (Thursday until 10 pm)... The first Sunday of the month is free for all

claim: Rue des Rosiers is the heart of Paris's historic Jewish quarter (the Pletzl), known for Sunday shopping, falafel, Middle Eastern restaurants, and pastry shops on narrow cobblestone streets.
quote: Rue des Rosiers is the heart of Paris's historic Jewish quarter, a charming, bustling street lined with delis, bakeries, and kosher restaurants, where you can sample some of the city's best falafel and challah bread.

claim: Le Marais is one of the few Paris neighborhoods where shops stay open on Sundays, allowing brunches, strolls, and gallery-hopping without shuttered storefronts.
quote: Le Marais is one of the few neighborhoods in Paris where everything stays open on Sundays, which means long brunches, slow strolls, and afternoons spent gallery-hopping without worrying about shuttered shops.

claim: On Sundays in the Marais many streets in the 4th arr are closed to cars, accessible only to pedestrians, bikes and roller-bladers; brunch peaks around noon.
quote: Most importantly about the Marais on Sunday is many of the streets in the 4th are closed off for pedestrians, bikes and roller-bladers.

claim: Place des Vosges is a 16th-century perfectly symmetrical square with fountains and arcades where Victor Hugo lived; Village Saint Paul is the antiques shopping zone.
quote: This '16th century square is one of the oldest squares in Paris.' It features 'perfectly symmetrical' design with 'beautiful fountains and fringed with trees,' surrounded by elegant townhouses and arcade restaurants. Victor Hugo famously lived here.

claim: Marais vintage shops range from luxury archives (Open Dressing — vintage Saint Laurent, Céline, Hermès) to by-the-kilo (Kilo Shop, a 500m² store selling jeans, kimonos, furs by weight) and chaotic classics (Free'p'star).
quote: Kilo Shop stands out because everything or almost everything is sold by the kilo—jeans, camouflage trousers, shirts, furs, scarves, bags, Japanese kimonos—in a 500m2 shop

claim: Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots were the meeting spots for Sartre, Simone de Beauvoir, Apollinaire, Camus, and Picasso in 20th-century Saint-Germain-des-Prés.
quote: Les Deux Magots and Café de Flore were regular meeting spots for the Paris literary and artistic world of the 20th century. Writers, painters, sculptors, musicians came here to work, converse, and find warmth and inspiration, including Jean-Paul Sartre, Simone de Beauvoir, Boris Vian, Guillaume Apollinaire, Albert Camus and Pablo Picasso.

claim: A Saint-Germain walking route runs from Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots through the church of St Germain, rue de l'Abbaye, Place de Fürstenberg, rue de Buci, up to rue de l'ancienne Comédie.
quote: Walking routes include the church of St Germain, rue De L'Abbaye, Place de Furstemberg, rue de Buci, up to rue de l'ancienne Comédie, and other historic streets.

claim: Montmartre is best before 9am — peaceful, gentle morning light on the Sacré-Cœur, few people on the basilica steps; midday Place du Tertre becomes a 'sea of people' and Sacré-Cœur lines stretch 'longer than the Seine'.
quote: The early morning is ideal, especially before 9am, when Montmartre is at its most peaceful, with the Sacré-Coeur illuminated by the gentle morning light.

claim: Locals advise against eating in Montmartre — it is 'tourist trap central' with some of the worst restaurants in Paris; visit Sacré-Cœur early then walk down the hill rather than up to avoid crowds.
quote: As a general rule, do not eat on Montmartre—tourist trap central. Some of the worst restaurants, not just in Paris, but anywhere.

claim: Clos Montmartre, in the 18th arr, is a real working vineyard created in 1933 with over 1,760 vines across 27 grape varieties (Gamay, Pinot); visits via Musée de Montmartre guided tours only.
quote: Created in 1933, Clos Montmartre comprises over 1,760 vines planted with 27 different grape varieties, including Gamay and Pinot.

claim: Musée de Montmartre, steps from Sacré-Cœur and Place du Tertre, includes Suzanne Valadon's studio and gardens overlooking the Clos Montmartre vineyard, inspired by Renoir's paintings made on site.
quote: the Montmartre museum and its gardens offer a haven of peace and greenery in the heart of Paris, where you can discover Suzanne Valadon's studio, the permanent collections, temporary exhibitions

claim: Canal Saint-Martin is one of Paris's most hipster/trendy neighborhoods, a local gem removed from tourist zones, with the 3-mile Quai de Valmy/Quai de Jemmapes walk and the locally beloved, tourist-overlooked Jardin Villemin as a picnic spot.
quote: the most hipster, trendy Paris neighborhoods

claim: Canal Saint-Martin evenings draw crowds to the embankments to drink wine; in summer locals picnic by the water with natural wine, cold cider, and snacks — try La Ciderie du Canal (51 Quai de Valmy), Combat for cocktails, or Le Comptoir Général.
quote: Evenings see hordes fill the embankments to drink wine and enjoy good company. In summer, locals stretch out by the water's edge with bottles of natural wine, cold ciders, and picnic snacks.

claim: A 2-hour Latin Quarter loop runs Quai de la Tournelle → Collège des Bernardins → Arènes de Lutèce → Grande Mosquée → Rue Mouffetard → Panthéon → Sorbonne → Shakespeare and Company → Square Viviani (Paris's oldest tree, 400+ years).
quote: Allow around 2 hours for this walk in the Latin Quarter, not including visits.

claim: Latin Quarter literary walks start at Shakespeare and Company, where Hemingway, Gertrude Stein, and Ezra Pound used to shop; the 1951 incarnation has hosted Beat Generation writers and 40,000+ travelers have slept among the books.
quote: Tours often start in front of the Shakespeare and Company bookstore, where Ernest Hemingway, Gertrude Stein, and Ezra Pound used to shop.

claim: Rue Mouffetard is the city's oldest market street; the Panthéon is the resting place of Victor Hugo, Voltaire, Rousseau, and the Curies; Place de la Contrescarpe is one of the liveliest student corners.
quote: Rue Mouffetard is one of the oldest streets in Paris and one of the most picturesque, with its food shops and restaurants. It is the city's oldest market street.

claim: Île Saint-Louis is the quieter, more authentic twin of Île de la Cité — 17th-century stone mansions, crooked streets, slower pace; Berthillon (rue Saint-Louis-en-l'Île, opened 1954) is closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
quote: the quieter, more charming twin of Île de la Cité

claim: Allow 1-2 hours to stroll rue Saint-Louis-en-l'Île; Berthillon at 31 has ~70 ice cream and sorbet flavors and reliable long lines; start at Pont Saint-Louis (the pedestrian bridge from Île de la Cité) where buskers play jazz and Piaf.
quote: Allow at least one to two hours to stroll Rue Saint-Louis-en-l'Île, explore the quays, visit a café, and enjoy an ice cream or glass of wine.

claim: Versailles 2026 Passport ticket is €35 high season (Apr 1–Oct 31), €25 low season; Palace closed Mondays, open 9:00–18:30; Passport includes timed Palace entry, Trianon, gardens with musical entertainment in high season.
quote: Low Season (Nov 1 - Mar 31): Standard €25 ... High Season (Apr 1 - Oct 31): Standard €35 ... Closed on Mondays and Décember 25th, January 1st and May 1st.

claim: The Passport is the only Versailles ticket that includes a timed Palace tour slot and grants access to the whole estate.
quote: The Passport is the optimal ticket as it offers access to the whole Estate and is the only ticket which includes a tour of the Palace with a fixed time slot.

claim: Versailles draws over 8 million visitors a year; May–June weekends are moderate-to-high crowd days; best days are Wednesday and Thursday, weekends and Tuesday (Louvre closed) are worst.
quote: over 8 million visitors a year ... Best days: Wednesday and Thursday. Avoid Tuesday (Louvre is closed Tuesday, pushing more visitors to Versailles) and weekends.

claim: RER C from central Paris reaches Versailles Château–Rive Gauche; weekend RER C summer maintenance can disrupt the line.
quote: Always check for RER C maintenance (especially summer weekends). Verify trains marked "VICK/VIRO" or similar to Versailles Château – Rive Gauche.

claim: Giverny is reached via Line J from Paris Saint-Lazare to Vernon (~50 min), then the SNGo shuttle bus (~10 min, €3 one way / ~€10 round trip).
quote: Paris to Vernon: Take Line J from Gare Saint-Lazare (~46 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes; €9–€22) ... Vernon to Giverny: Board the SNGo shuttle bus (~10 minutes; €3).

claim: Giverny water lilies start blooming in late May and peak through June, opening in the morning and closing in the afternoon — June is the single best month if visiting only once.
quote: Water lilies start blooming in late May and peak through June ... if you can only go once, go in June.

claim: Monet's House and Gardens are open daily April 1 to November 1, 2026, 10:00–18:00 (last entry 17:30); advance booking strongly recommended May–August.
quote: Monet's House and Gardens are open daily from 1 April to 1 November 2026 ... 10:00am to 6:00pm, with last admission at 5:30pm ... booking in advance is strongly recommended, especially if you're visiting between May and August.

claim: Fontainebleau is reached via Transilien Line R from Gare de Lyon to Fontainebleau–Avon (~40 min, trains every ~30 min), then Bus Line 1 to the Château stop.
quote: Take the train from Paris Gare de Lyon ... towards Montargis, Montereau, or Laroche-Migennes, and get off at the Fontainebleau-Avon station. The journey takes approximately 40–45 minutes. Trains run approximately every 30 minutes.

claim: Fontainebleau château adult entry is €14 (Grands Appartements + Napoleon I Museum); courtyards and gardens are free; closed Tuesdays.
quote: Entry tickets cost €14 per adult (includes Grands Appartements and Napoleon I Museum). Courtyards and gardens are free and open every day ... closed every day except Tuesday.

claim: Fontainebleau was a royal residence for 700+ years — longer than Versailles — and is recommended specifically for travelers who want to skip the Versailles crowds.
quote: This royal palace was home to French monarchs for over 700 years — longer than Versailles ... If the idea of fighting crowds at Versailles doesn't appeal to you, Fontainebleau is your answer.

claim: Forêt de Fontainebleau surrounds the château with hundreds of sandstone boulders and 20,000+ climbing problems plus marked hiking trails (4-hour yellow loop), making it a combined château + nature day.
quote: The forest of Fontainebleau boasts hundreds of boulders and more than 20,000 problems ... There is a trail marked in yellow which takes around 4 hours to complete.

claim: Chantilly is reached by hourly trains from Gare du Nord (Grandes Lignes, platforms 9–18) in about 20–25 minutes to Chantilly-Gouvieux; a free shuttle covers the 10-minute hop from station to château.
quote: The train Paris–Chantilly leaves from Gare du Nord train station hourly, from the Grandes Lignes area (platforms 9 to 18) ... count it for taking 20 minutes ... free shuttle that runs from the train station to the château ... the ride takes about 10 minutes.

claim: Chantilly pairs the Condé Museum (second-largest collection of antique paintings in France after the Louvre, three Raphaels) with the Great Stables / Living Museum of the Horse; château open Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00.
quote: the second largest museum of antique paintings in France after the Louvre, the Conde Museum collections ... the only French museum to own three Raphael paintings other than the Louvre ... The Great Stables of Chantilly houses the Living Museum of the Horse.

claim: Reims is ~46 min by TGV from Gare de l'Est, tickets from ~€27 one-way booked ahead; cathedral, Champagne houses (Taittinger, Veuve Clicquot, Pommery) and old town fit in 5–6 hours, so a half/full-day is feasible.
quote: Paris Gare de l'Est and the high-speed trains take 46 minutes to get to Reims. Tickets start from around €27 each way if you book in advance ... You can easily cover the cathedral, champagne cellars, and old town in 5-6 hours.

claim: Provins is a UNESCO-listed medieval walled town ~80–90 minutes from Paris by train+bus, with ramparts, underground galleries and falconry/equestrian shows; the Médiévales festival weekend in 2026 is June 13–14.
quote: In about 80 to 90 minutes, you can leave the capital behind and step into a UNESCO-listed medieval town ... In 2026, the headline weekend falls on June 13 and 14.

claim: Standard interest-based shortlist places palace fans at Versailles or Fontainebleau, art lovers at Giverny or Chantilly's Condé Museum — Giverny is explicitly seasonal (late March to early November).
quote: Palace fans: Versailles (blockbuster), Fontainebleau (less crowded) ... Art lovers: Giverny, Auvers-sur-Oise, Chantilly (Condé Museum) ... Giverny is seasonal (late March to early November).

claim: Three Paris bars made the World's 50 Best Bars 2025 list: Bar Nouveau (#17), The Cambridge Public House (#20), and Danico (#30).
quote: Bar Nouveau - Ranked 17th (previously 39th in 2024); The Cambridge Public House - Ranked 20th (previously 19th in 2024); Danico - Ranked 30th (previously 49th in 2024)

claim: Bar Nouveau is an Art Nouveau-inspired walk-in-only cocktail bar at 5 Rue des Haudriettes in the 3rd, a mainstay in the World's 50 Best top 20.
quote: Bar Nouveau is a mainstay in the world's top 50 list (right now it's 17th). Despite the accolades, it's walk-in only, meaning a shot at a coveted seat.

claim: Bar Hemingway at the Ritz Paris specializes in bespoke cocktails built around the guest's mood — no fixed menu — with the Serendipity and Dry Martini invented on-site.
quote: At the intimate Bar Hemingway, the great writer's legend is reborn every evening, among upholstered leathers and sepia lights... celebrated Serendipity, invented right here, and the Dry Martini

claim: Cravan occupies a 1911 Hector Guimard-designed Art Nouveau building classed as a national historic monument and is one of Paris's top cocktail rooms in 2026.
quote: Cravan - Located in the 16th arrondissement, Cravan is one of the best bars in the city, housed in a 1911 Art Nouveau building designed by Hector Guimard that is classed as a national 'historic monument'.

claim: Bisou is a no-menu bespoke cocktail bar at 15 boulevard du Temple in the 3rd; bartenders build drinks from guests' moods and seasonal ingredients.
quote: Bisou doesn't have a menu — instead, bartenders craft bespoke cocktails based on guests' tastes, preferences, and moods using seasonal ingredients.

claim: Combat is a female-owned Belleville cocktail bar with reasonably priced (€10-14) inventive cocktails using homemade bitters and tinctures, laid-back and unpretentious.
quote: Combat is a light and airy, minimalist space with foliage hanging from the ceiling... cocktails are affordable at 10-12€ for excellent drinks... no/low-ABV cocktails, natural wines, and beer.

claim: Terrass" Hotel in Montmartre offers a 7th-floor panoramic rooftop with nighttime views of the Eiffel Tower, Louvre and Sacré-Coeur, ideal for evening drinks.
quote: Dramatically positioned atop Montmartre's highest point with panoramic views. The nighttime vista includes the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Sacré-Coeur, making it ideal for evening drinks.

claim: The Galeries Lafayette 7th-floor rooftop is free-entry and a prime sunset spot, with the Eiffel Tower silhouette darkening against a pastel sky at golden hour.
quote: this free-entry rooftop is a favorite with locals and visitors alike... As golden hour paints Paris in honey tones, more people gather to watch the show – the Eiffel Tower silhouette darkening against a pastel sky

claim: Le Perchoir Ménilmontant is a bohemian-chic rooftop with 360-degree views especially striking at sunset over Sacré-Coeur.
quote: Perched on top of an old industrial building close to the Ménilmontant metro station, Le Perchoir is a charming and bohemian chic rooftop bar & restaurant with amazing 360º views over Paris, extra special when the sun sets over the Sacré-Coeur.

claim: The Eiffel Tower sparkles for 5 minutes on the hour after nightfall, running until midnight (1am in summer), using 20,000 6W bulbs strobing in rapid sequence.
quote: First sparkle typically starts on the full hour following sunset; Repeats hourly until midnight (1:00 a.m. in summer); Uses '20,000 6 W bulbs strobing in very rapid sequence'

claim: Trocadéro and Pont de Bir-Hakeim are top sparkle viewpoints; arrive 40-90 minutes early for prime spots, and in 2026 the Pont d'Iéna is now a pedestrianized green bridge dedicated to sparkle viewing.
quote: As of 2026, the area between Trocadéro and the Eiffel Tower has been fully reimagined, with the Pont d'Iéna now a 'green bridge' dedicated to pedestrians and cyclists, providing a stable, central, and free location to watch the sparkle.

claim: Les Deux Magots in Saint-Germain-des-Prés is open daily 7:30 to 01:00, making it a viable late-evening aperitif terrace facing the church.
quote: Les Deux Magots café is open daily from 7:30 to 01:00, making it suitable for breakfast, lunch and late drinks.

claim: A typical Paris jazz evening pairs a 9:30pm set at one of the rue des Lombards clubs (Duc, Sunset/Sunside, Le Baiser Salé) with the post-midnight swing party at Caveau de la Huchette across the river.
quote: A great evening looks like a 9:30 PM show on rue des Lombards, then a walk across the river to catch the last hour of swing at the Caveau, where the party runs well past midnight.

claim: Le Duc des Lombards hosts roughly 300 shows a year and offers free late-night jam sessions after 11:30pm, ideal for post-dinner jazz.
quote: Le Duc des Lombards hosts around 300 shows every year, including nightly performances and late-night jams. Free late-night jams after 11:30 PM are available at this venue.

claim: Crazy Horse is the sophisticated-visitor cabaret pick — artistic nude performance in an intimate 400-seat theatre — while the Lido has closed (now Lido 2 music hall) and Moulin Rouge remains the spectacle option.
quote: Crazy Horse is positioned for adults seeking refined entertainment... 'Artistic nude performance' in an 'Intimate, sophisticated atmosphere'... an intimately small theatre housing only 400 guests, compared to Moulin Rouge's 850-seat capacity.

claim: Cabaret tickets run from €150/person base, with dinner+show packages €180-250; the dinner is mediocre and seating position is critical at Moulin Rouge.
quote: Budget €150 per person minimum for any of them (that's base ticket). Dinner + show packages run €180-250... Dinner is mediocre—you're paying for the show, not the food.

claim: A standard Bateaux Mouches sightseeing cruise is €18 for 1 hour 10 minutes; Vedettes du Pont Neuf is around €17 for 1 hour and offers smaller, more intimate boats with live commentary — both are timed for the Eiffel Tower lights.
quote: Vedettes du Pont Neuf... cost about 17 euro per person, last an hour, and have live commentary... Operates with smaller-sized boats creating a more intimate and friendly atmosphere... the cruise is timed for the Eiffel Tower lights

claim: Travel forums consistently recommend the standard evening sightseeing cruise over the dinner cruise, which divides attention between food and scenery.
quote: Avoid dinner cruises because it divides your attention between the scenery and food, and the sightseeing cruises are considered one of the best bargains in Paris.

claim: Les Berges de Seine is a 2.3km pedestrian-only walkway on the Left Bank from Pont de l'Alma to Pont Royal — a former urban highway converted to gardens, bars and restaurants.
quote: Les Berges de Seine is a pedestrian-only walkway following the left bank of the Seine River, with a 2.3 kilometer path which is about 1.5 miles. Les Berges de Seine leads from the Pont de L'Alma (near the Eiffel Tower) to the Pont Royal (near the Musée D'Orsay).

claim: Pont des Arts between the Institut de France and the Louvre is a romantic pedestrian-only bridge especially atmospheric at sunset with buskers and street artists; it is under construction May 4-June 11 2026 but remains pedestrian-accessible.
quote: Especially in the evening, around sunset, the bridge's reputation as one of the most romantic places in Paris is enhanced by buskers and street artists... The Pont des Arts is under construction from May 4 to June 11, 2026, but remains accessible to pedestrians (exclusively) during the works.

claim: Maison Souquet's hidden bar in Montmartre (9th, 2 min from Moulin Rouge) serves Sade-inspired cocktails like the Castiglione (€16) in a 'desire red' atmosphere — a late-night refuge styled after a courtesan's parlour.
quote: The bar is the new intimate and secret refuge of all the Parisiennes and hip dandies who come delve in the 'desire red' atmosphere and sip heady potions. Wild cocktails, inspired by Sade and the names of great courtesans such as the Castiglione... are available at 16€.

claim: Berthillon on Île Saint-Louis (29-31 rue Saint-Louis en l'Île) is widely regarded as the best ice cream in Paris, with the wild strawberry sorbet (fraise des bois) as its signature.
quote: For nearly 70 years now, the Berthillon family has been serving sorbets, ice creams, and pastries out of the quaint wood-panelled storefront. Continually hailed as the best ice cream in Paris... try the wild strawberry sorbet, sorbet à la fraise des bois — it's how Berthillon first gained fame.

claim: 2026 Paris transit fares: single Metro/RER ticket €2.55, bus/tram €2.05, airport access €14, Navigo Jour day pass €12.30, Navigo Easy card €2.
quote: Metro/RER/Train: €2.55 ... Bus/Tram: €2.05 ... Airport access: €14.00 ... Day pass (Navigo Jour): €12.30 ... Paris Visite 1-day: €30.60 ... Navigo Easy card (reloadable): €2.00

claim: Magnetic paper t+ tickets stop working on buses in May 2026 and across the rail network in June 2026, so visitors must use a Navigo Easy card or the RATP/Île-de-France Mobilités smartphone app.
quote: Paper tickets are officially dead. Magnetic paper tickets will stop working on buses in May 2026 and on the entire rail network — metro, RER, and trains — in June 2026.

claim: Paris Visite pass 2026: €30.60 (1d), €45.40 (2d), €63.80 (3d), €78.00 (5d), covering all five zones including airport access, Orlyval, Disneyland and Versailles.
quote: Paris Visite ... 1 day: €30.60 ... 2 days: €45.40 ... 3 days: €63.80 ... 5 days: €78.00 ... unlimited travel in Paris and the Île-de-France region, including access to Paris airports, Orlyval, Disneyland Paris and the Palace of Versailles.

claim: Navigo Easy is a reusable contactless card sold at metro ticket windows/machines for €2 (non-refundable); single tickets at €2.55 can be loaded individually and the card no longer carries a discount on ten-packs as of Jan 1, 2026.
quote: as of Jan. 1, 2026 booklets of ten Metro-Train-RER tickets no longer have a quantity discount from the full price even if put on a Navigo Easy card.

claim: Métro Line 14, extended south on 24 June 2024 to Aéroport d'Orly, now reaches Châtelet in central Paris in about 25 minutes, replacing the older OrlyVal/RER B connection for Orly arrivals.
quote: The Orly Airport train to Paris on Metro 14 will take 25 minutes between Orly Airport and Chatelet (in the heart of Paris close to the Louvre).

claim: From CDG in 2026: official fixed-fare taxis are €56 (Right Bank) / €65 (Left Bank), RER B costs €14 to central Paris in ~35 min, and the legacy Roissybus shut down 1 March 2026, replaced by Line 9517 routed via Saint-Denis Pleyel rather than Opéra.
quote: Fixed-rate taxis cost €56 to the Right Bank or €65 to the Left Bank ... The RER B train is €14 ... On March 1, 2026, the direct bus between CDG and the Opéra neighborhood shut down permanently after 34 years.

claim: Métro Line 1 (Charles de Gaulle-Étoile to Châtelet-Les Halles) is the single most pickpocketed stretch in Paris, with the Châtelet–Les Halles interchange the top targeted station; Line 6 (Trocadéro–Nation) also flagged.
quote: Metro Line 1 between Charles de Gaulle-Etoile and Chatelet-Les Halles is the most pickpocketed stretch in Paris ... Line 1 (Châtelet to La Défense corridor) and Line 6 (Trocadéro to Nation) see the highest activity.

claim: Common Paris tourist scams in 2026 include the friendship-bracelet trick at Sacré-Cœur (wrist grabbed, bracelet tied, $10–20 demanded), fake deaf-mute petition pickpocket teams near Notre-Dame/Louvre/Eiffel, and the dropped-gold-ring 'reward' scam.
quote: Men near Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre grab tourists' wrists and quickly tie a bracelet before they can refuse, then demand $10–20 per bracelet.

claim: US State Department keeps France at Level 2 (exercise increased caution) for 2026 due to terrorism and civil-unrest risk, and explicitly flags pickpocket and phone-theft activity in airports, stations, the metro and tourist sites — often by under-16 operatives working in groups.
quote: Pickpocketing and phone thefts are common, especially in crowded places ... it is common for pickpockets in Paris to be under the age of 16, as they are less likely to face arrest/prosecution. Professional pickpockets often work in pairs or larger groups.

claim: Late-May Paris weather typically peaks near 20°C with around 15 rain days and 62 mm rainfall across the month, but 2026 has seen an unprecedented heat streak with the hottest May day on record on 26 May.
quote: temperatures tend to warm up, reaching an average of 20.3°C by the end of May ... There are usually 15 days with some rain in Paris in May and the average monthly rainfall is 62mm ... France recorded its hottest May day since records began on May 26, 2026.

claim: Paris daylight lengthens from ~14h39 to ~15h56 across May, with late-May sunset around 21:43; civil twilight extends usable light another ~45 minutes after sunset.
quote: The day length increases by 1 hour, 16 minutes over the course of May 2026 in Paris, ranging from 14 hours, 39 minutes on the first day to 15 hours, 56 minutes on the last day.

claim: Most non-tourist Paris shops are closed Sunday, but seven designated tourist zones — including the Marais, Champs-Élysées, rue de Rivoli, boulevard Saint-Germain and Montmartre — are exempt and trade on Sunday year-round.
quote: Paris has seven 'tourist zones' - including the Champs Elysées, the rue de Rivoli, the boulevard Saint Germain, Montmartre and the Marais, where shops can open on Sundays.

claim: Vélib' short-term passes cost €5/day for mechanical bikes and €10/day for e-bikes (with €1/€2 per extra 30 min); tourists register through the Vélib' app or at a station kiosk and the network covers ~1,400+ stations across Paris.
quote: The price for a full day is €5 for a regular bicycle and €10 for an electric bicycle, with additional charges of €1 per 30 minutes for a regular bicycle and €2 for an electric bicycle.

claim: From July 2026 Paris opens 11 free public swimming sites — three of them directly in the Seine at Bercy, Bras de Grenelle and Pont Louis-Philippe — staffed with lifeguards and showers, as a lasting Olympic legacy after a 100-year swim ban.
quote: From July 2026, Paris will be welcoming freshwater enthusiasts with officially authorized swimming in the Seine and other urban bodies of water ... Three new sites in the Seine include Bercy (12th arrondissement), Louis-Philippe (4th arrondissement) ... and Bras de Grenelle (15th arrondissement).

claim: Other Paris-2024 legacy gains visible by 2026 include the pedestrianised Place de la Concorde and continued public use of Olympic ceremony bridges such as Pont d'Iéna, plus the cleaned-up Seine quays now repurposed for sports and fan events.
quote: the Pont d'Iéna welcomed visitors from around the world to walk in the footsteps of Paris 2024 champions ... it kept its sporty spirit alive, serving as a temporary fan zone during the latest edition of the Roland-Garros tennis tournament.

claim: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont in the 19th is a 25-hectare hilly park beloved by locals for picnics, t'ai chi, puppet shows and sundown wine, with views of Sacré-Coeur from its cliffs.
quote: It's a favourite with Parisians, who come here to practice t'ai chi, take the kids to a puppet show or simply to relax with a bottle of wine and a sundown picnic.

claim: Marché des Enfants Rouges at 39 rue de Bretagne in the 3rd is the oldest covered market in Paris, established in 1628 and listed as a historic monument since 1982; named after a nearby orphanage where children wore red.
quote: The Marché des Enfants Rouges is the oldest covered market in Paris, France. It was established in 1628 as the petit marché du Marais... listed as a historic monument since 1982.

claim: Marché des Enfants Rouges is a working lunchtime spot — visitors are warned to avoid weekday lunch hour when nearby office workers descend on it.
quote: try to avoid the lunch hour on weekdays when Parisians from the nearby office buildings descend upon the market for lunch.

claim: Butte-aux-Cailles in the 13th keeps a village-like character with cobbled streets, low houses and ivy, and has become Paris's epicentre of intimate street art — stencils by Miss.Tic, Seth Globepainter and Levalet on doors, windows and electrical boxes.
quote: more intimate works: sharp stencils, paste-ups, handwritten texts, and small illustrations hidden on doors, windows, and electrical boxes... Miss.Tic... Seth Globepainter... Levalet

claim: The Coulée verte René-Dumont (Promenade Plantée) in the 12th is a 4.7 km elevated linear park opened in 1993 on a disused railway viaduct — the first project worldwide to repurpose elevated rail into urban garden, predating NYC's High Line by 16 years.
quote: Coulée verte René-Dumont... 4.7 km (2.9 mi) elevated linear park built on top of obsolete railway infrastructure in the 12th arrondissement

claim: National Geographic frames the Promenade Plantée as the original elevated park that inspired NYC's High Line, running from Bastille through the 12th past the Viaduc des Arts.
quote: How to explore Promenade Plantée in Paris, France

claim: Marché Bastille on Boulevard Richard-Lenoir runs Thursday and Sunday mornings (around 7am–3pm) with roughly a hundred traders — among the biggest and liveliest open-air markets in central Paris.
quote: On Thursday and Sunday mornings, around a hundred traders offer a wide range of products in a friendly atmosphere.

claim: Printemps Haussmann's 7th-floor terrasse du 7e Ciel is free during store hours (Mon–Sat 10:00–20:00, Sun 11:00–20:00) and gives a panorama from the Opéra Garnier across to the Eiffel Tower.
quote: panoramic terrace on the 7th floor of Le Printemps Femme offers a sublime view from the Opera to the Eiffel Tower... free of charge during the department store's opening hours

claim: The Institut du Monde Arabe's 9th-floor rooftop in the 5th is free and open 10:00–18:00 daily, offering close-up views of Notre-Dame and the Seine that most tourists miss.
quote: The Institut du Monde Arabe offers free access to a panoramic terrace... ideal vantage point over the Seine and Notre-Dame de Paris.

claim: Tour Saint-Jacques (4th, near Châtelet) opens for guided climbs Wed–Sun May to November, by reservation only — 300+ steep steps to a 54m summit with unbroken views of Sacré-Coeur, Eiffel Tower and Notre-Dame; €12 full / €10 reduced.
quote: Guided tours are offered by MagmaCultura... 54 meters above ground, Paris spreads out before you... taking in the Sacré-Coeur, the Eiffel Tower and Notre-Dame.

claim: Belleville (20th/19th/10th/11th borders) is Paris's alternative neighbourhood — student-and-artist territory dominated by street art, pubs and galleries rather than boutiques, retaining village-like solidarity and an aperitif culture at institutions like Aux Folies and Café Chéri(e).
quote: the lively Paris of students, artists and families from all over the world, where street art, pubs, and galleries dominate

claim: Michelin Guide notes Belleville defies Paris trends, with locals gathering for an apéro before nightlife at Place Maurice Chevalier and along Rue Dénoyez.
quote: A Guide to Belleville, the Paris Neighborhood That Defies Trends

claim: Père Lachaise in the 20th is the world's most-visited cemetery — over 3 million visitors a year — free to enter, open 8:00–18:00 (5:30pm in winter), and home to Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde and Édith Piaf among others.
quote: Père Lachaise cemetery, the most visited cemetery in the world.

claim: Oscar Wilde's tomb at Père Lachaise was so covered in lipstick kisses that cemetery workers built a glass barrier around it; Édith Piaf's family grave (marked Famille Gassion-Piaf) is tricky to find and rewarding for it.
quote: Oscar Wilde's stone grave was once so covered in lipstick kisses that cemetery workers encased it in a glass barrier.

claim: Rue Crémieux is a 144m pedestrian street in the 12th with pastel-painted 19th-century worker houses (repainted from 1996), one of the most Instagrammed spots in Paris with 30,000+ tagged posts by 2019 — and residents have asked the city to gate it on weekends because of the photo crowds.
quote: By 2019, Rue Crémieux had become one of the most Instagrammed locations in Paris, with over 30,000 posts tagged #ruecremieux.

claim: W Magazine reported residents of Rue Crémieux actively try to shame Instagram crowds and have lobbied for a closing gate — a flag that the street is more a curiosity than a peaceful detour.
quote: Paris Residents Are Trying to Banish Instagram Hordes From Their Cute Pastel Rue Crémieux

claim: Bois de Vincennes east of Paris (2,459 acres / largest green space in the city) is the locals' weekend picnic default — verdant lawns by Lac Daumesnil and Lac des Minimes, plus a Buddhist temple, zoo and rowboat rentals.
quote: The Bois de Vincennes is Paris' largest green lung, at 2,459 acres... a favorite among locals for weekend picnics. The best spots are on the verdant lawns near Lac Daumesnil or Lac des Minimes.

claim: Bois de Boulogne (846 ha — bigger than Central Park or Hyde Park) on the west edge of Paris is a major picnic and weekend escape, with two lakes, cascades and dedicated picnic areas.
quote: Plan a picnic in Paris - The best spots

claim: Parc Monceau in the 8th is an English-style park (1778, commissioned by the Duke of Chartres) with curved paths, a Roman colonnade, pyramid and dotted statues — popular with locals from the surrounding posh neighbourhood for jogging and reading.
quote: the park reflected the Duke's fascination with exoticism and featured whimsical elements like a pyramid, a Roman colonnade, and a Dutch windmill.

claim: The Philharmonie de Paris / Cité de la Musique in the 19th (Parc de la Villette) runs the Orchestre de Paris 2025/26 season with 49 symphonic concerts, plus visiting orchestras like LSO under Simon Rattle (31 May 2026) and Sächsische Staatskapelle Dresden under Daniele Gatti (29 May 2026).
quote: Agenda | Philharmonie de Paris

claim: Palais Garnier in the 9th can be visited as a self-guided tour (~€15, daily 10:00–17:00, last entry 16:30) separately from any ballet/opera ticket; the Paris Opera Ballet's main season runs roughly September–June.
quote: Visit The Palais Garnier - Opéra national de Paris
